note: The one authority for BoltBeam's plain words, read only through report/plain.py. stages: the plain name of every pipeline stage key, the report's and the measuring ones ({here} is this machine's name); the TUI reads this table, and roles, through `screen words`. roles and parts: what a row of the where table is called in layer 1 and 2. role_parts: the word for one shape of a role the model holds at two shapes of one format when its fine role does not tell them apart (a mixer's down and up, an indexer's q and k). templates: layer 1 of each run type, as format strings over numbers the results already hold. figures: the labels under layer 1's headline figures (tok/s, ms, s and %, the units in `units`). not_parts: the where-table rows that are not a part of the model's work, by the row's `what` or its name (BoltBeam's own gaps: the balance of the limit, the rest not split, kernels no kind names); `unassigned` are the weight reads no part took, said once as a caveat with their time, never as a part. head_to_head: the compare view's rows, the line that says what differs, and why the parts are or are not compared. tools and engines: the toolchain's and the engines' own names, as their makers spell them. trust: the one trust line. measured: the sentences of 'How it was measured'. glossary: every term layer 2 cannot avoid, each explained once; a term's `match` words are what layer 2 is searched for. roles names every role of the role vocabulary (vocab.RoleClass and RoleGroup); report_roles are the ones report.html's Full detail names, kept apart so that page stays as it was. Every reason a run gives in its own words has a key; layer 1 and 'How it was measured' say the key's sentence here, and the run's own words stay in Full detail.

offload.close_band: {pct}% of the fastest this GPU and this machine's memory allow with the experts kept in RAM ({limit} tok/s). The range is because it depends on how often the needed parts are already on the card, and this run did not report that.
offload.close_one: {pct}% of the fastest this GPU and this machine's memory allow with the experts kept in RAM ({limit} tok/s).
offload.estimate: This is an estimate: the model's shapes were not read from a header.
offload.over: Faster than the limit it was held against ({limit} tok/s), so that limit is wrong for this run; no percentage is shown.
offload.none: There is no limit for this run yet: it kept experts in RAM, so the limit for a model held in GPU memory does not apply, and {reason}.
offload.decode_tuned: This setup is tuned for writing replies: with the experts in RAM a long prompt is read 5 to 18 times slower than with the whole model on the card (measured on an RTX 5090).
offload.unrecorded: Placement not recorded: this run did not say whether the experts were on the card or in RAM.
offload.for_decode: For writing replies (decode): every expert in RAM, a cache of the ones in use on the card.
offload.for_prefill: For reading prompts (prefill): whole layers' experts on the card, the rest in RAM, a larger chunk.
offload.prefill_tuned: This setup is tuned for reading prompts: a prompt never hits the expert cache, so the card holds whole layers instead, and a larger chunk uploads each expert once for more tokens.
offload.cpu_figure: of each token at least, for the experts the processor computes from RAM (not GPU time)
offload.cpu_experts: The experts the processor computes from RAM are their own part: they are not GPU time and not GPU memory reads, so a GPU capture sees them only as gaps between kernels.

offload_page.title: Offload: running a model past GPU memory
offload_page.fits_card: The whole model fits on the card, so nothing needs to go to RAM; this is what offloading would give.
offload_page.past_card: The model does not fit on the card: part of it has to live in RAM.
offload_page.card_replies: {dense} dense parts + {kv} KV cache + a {cache} cache of experts = {used} of {usable} usable
offload_page.ram_replies_cached: every expert, {experts}, read once to fill the card's cache
offload_page.card_prompts: {dense} dense parts + {kv} KV cache + the experts of {on} of {layers} layers ({experts}) = {used} of {usable} usable
offload_page.ram_prompts_none: no experts: every layer's experts fit on the card
offload_page.tables: {tables}: the model's input embeddings, not counted in the RAM above: the engine maps them from disk and the system keeps the rows it reads, so under memory pressure they compete with the experts for RAM
offload_page.spill: {spill} more than the usable RAM: the engine would read it from disk, which no limit here covers
offload_page.spill_if_offloaded: only if you choose to offload: {spill} more than the usable RAM, which the engine would read from disk, and no limit here covers that
offload_page.set_replies: every expert in RAM, a {mib} MiB cache of the ones in use on the card, the processor computes {pct}% of the misses
offload_page.set_replies_cached: every expert in RAM and all of them in a {mib} MiB cache on the card, so there are no misses to compute or copy
offload_page.set_prompts: the experts of {n} of {layers} layers in RAM, chunks of {ubatch} tokens
offload_page.set_prompts_none: every expert on the card, chunks of {ubatch} tokens
offload_page.replies_limit: at most {span} {unit}, depending on how often the needed experts are already on the card
offload_page.replies_limit_cached: at most {span} {unit}: every expert is in the card's cache
offload_page.replies_limit_flat: at most {span} {unit}, however often the needed experts are already on the card
offload_page.prompts_limit: at most {tok_s} tok/s reading a {prompt}-token prompt; writing replies with this setup, at most {replies} tok/s
offload_page.bound_gpu: reading weights from GPU memory at {gbs} GB/s
offload_page.bound_cpu: the processor reading experts from RAM at {gbs} GB/s
offload_page.bound_link_pageable: copies from normal memory at {gbs} GB/s
offload_page.bound_link_wire: copies to the card at the link's {gbs} GB/s (not measured: an upper bound)
offload_page.bound_link_reported: copies to the card at the link's reported {gbs} GB/s (not measured)
offload_page.unmeasured_wire: {short} at the link's wire rate, an upper bound: no measured host-to-device rate
offload_page.unmeasured_reported: {short} at the link's reported speed: no measured host-to-device rate
offload_page.no_rate: no copy to the GPU was measured and {the}'s speed was not read, so there is no rate for the experts it copies: run boltbeam host on an idle GPU
offload_page.direct_read_prompts: the experts read in place over the link are still counted as GPU-memory reads in the prompt limit's GPU rows, so that part is an upper estimate of the time
offload_page.pinned_gap: An engine that pins its host memory copies at {pinned} GB/s here, against {pageable} GB/s from normal memory (both measured on this GPU).
offload_page.pinned_prompts: Reading prompts with this setup: at most {now} tok/s now, at most {then} tok/s with pinned copies.
offload_page.pinned_prompts_none: Reading prompts with this setup copies nothing (every expert is on the card), so pinned copies would not change it.
offload_page.pinned_replies: Writing replies with every miss copied (no processor share): at most {now} tok/s now, {then} tok/s with pinned copies.
offload_page.pinned_replies_none: Writing replies with this setup copies nothing after loading (every expert is in the card's cache), so pinned copies would not change it.
offload_page.pinned_caveat: These are limits, not promises: llama.cpp copies from normal memory, and an engine with pinned copies still has to keep them busy.
offload_page.pinned_unmeasured: No pinned copy rate was measured here ({why}), so the gap cannot be stated.
offload_page.ram_now_unknown: {total} in all; how much is available could not be read
offload_page.copies_none: none needed: unified memory, the GPU reads the same memory as the CPU
offload_page.shared_memory: this GPU shares the CPU's memory, so there is no separate card memory to keep experts out of: the whole model must fit the shared memory, and its limit is the ordinary one
offload_page.copies: {pageable} GB/s from normal memory, {pinned} GB/s from pinned memory (measured on this GPU, {when})
offload_page.copies_unmeasured: not measured; the link's {gbs} GB/s stands in, an upper bound
offload_page.copies_unmeasured_reported: not measured; the link's reported {gbs} GB/s stands in

engine_upgrade.upgrade: This run used a new {engine} build; it was compared once with the previous one ({before}).

compare.replay_close: {points} points of the fastest this GPU allows.
compare.unchanged: unchanged outside the parts that moved
compare.not_checked: not checked: no repeat runs of the earlier build

gain.tok_s: {gain} tok/s if this ran at full speed
gain.ms: {gain} ms faster if this ran at full speed
gain.none_over: Gains per part aren't shown: recording slowed the run by more than {ceiling}%, too much to share out the lost time fairly.
gain.none_unqualified: Gains per part aren't shown: the recording's timing was not checked against the run without it.
gain.none_estimate: Gains per part aren't shown: the parts were timed alone, not inside the run.
gain.none_unmatched: Gains per part aren't shown: the recording kept no timing that matches the run without it, so its per-part times can't be checked against the real speed.
gain.unassigned: {ms} ms of weight reads could not be matched to a part.

trust.checked_how: the parts add up to the measured time
trust.within_overhead: recording slowed the run by {pct}%, under the {ceiling}% allowed
trust.refused: Not checked: a part's time broke one of the report's rules, so the parts are not shown (Full detail says which).
trust.estimate: The split by part is an estimate: each part was timed alone, outside the engine.
trust.over_overhead: Recording slowed the run by {pct}%, more than the {ceiling}% allowed, so gains per part aren't shown.
trust.unqualified: The recording's timing was not checked against the run without it, so gains per part aren't shown.
trust.unpaired: Some GPU work could not be matched to a part of the model.
trust.left_out: Some parts are left out of the totals: {parts}.
trust.no_graph: The engine's graph replay failed, so this run is slower than the engine usually is.
trust.whole_only: Only the speed is measured, so there is nothing yet to check it against.
trust.unmatched: The recording kept no timing that matches the run without it, so gains per part aren't shown.

measured.speed: The speed is the engine running on its own, with nothing recording it, {how}.
measured.in_model: Each part was timed inside the real run, recorded with {tool}.
measured.isolated: Each part's GPU code was timed alone, outside the engine, then fitted to the real run's time.
measured.captured: Each part was timed inside the real run, split by the engine's own labels.
measured.replicated: The recording was repeated {captures} times; the parts agree within {worst}% (the rule allows {tolerance}%).
measured.not_replicated: The recording was repeated {captures} times and the parts disagree by up to {worst}% (the rule allows {tolerance}%).
measured.overhead: Recording slowed the run by {pct}% (the limit is {ceiling}%).
measured.overhead_rows: The part times still stand, because the repeated recordings agree; the idle time is shown as at most what the unrecorded run leaves.
measured.overhead_ms: Without recording a step took {untraced} ms; recording changed it by {diff} ms.
measured.repeats: No repeat runs of this exact setup yet, so how much these numbers vary from run to run is not known.
measured.band: This setup has repeat runs; how far apart they were is in Full detail.
measured.module_load: Where some of the engine's GPU code lives was found in one more run of the same program, outside the timed ones.
measured.forced: Every recorded pass was made to produce the same tokens, so the labels and the times are of the same steps.
measured.graph: The engine's graph replay failed on this run, so it ran without it.
measured.clock: The GPU's clock speed during the run was recorded (Full detail).
measured.speculation: The model drafted tokens ahead; how many drafts were accepted is in Full detail.
measured.limit: The limit is the time to read every byte this step needs once, at this GPU's measured memory speed ({gbs} GB/s); no real run can be faster.
measured.limit_ops: The limit is the sum of each recorded part's own fastest time on this GPU.
measured.gains: The gains share out the lost time by how long each part takes; they add up to the limit, but they are not promised speed-ups.
measured.no_model: A part with no limit of its own counts all of its time as lost.
measured.upgrade: This build was compared once with the previous one (Full detail).
measured.sweep: The batch sweep's best was {best} tok/s in all, with {best_batch} streams at a context of {best_context} tokens; the figures above are the run the parts were timed on.

glossary.plain: Tokens a second: how many words (or pieces of words) the model writes each second. Higher is faster.
The fastest this GPU allows for this model: the time to move every byte the step needs once at the GPU's memory speed (or, for heavy maths, at its top compute speed). A real run is always slower.
Milliseconds: thousandths of a second.
How many tokens of conversation the model already holds when it writes the next one. More context means more to read.
One conversation. A GPU can serve several at once (a batch); each gets its own tokens.
The text the model reads before it starts to reply. Reading it is called prefill.
One piece of the model's work in each step, such as the feed-forward or attention layers, or the time between GPU steps.
How long this part takes now, in each token (or each step of several streams, or each prompt).
This part's share of the lost time: of all the time the run takes beyond the limit, how much is in this part.
What this part would give back if it ran at its own limit: its share of the distance from the measured speed to the limit.
The speed with this part and every part above it fixed.
A part's time now, less its time at the limit.
The fastest this kind of work can run on this GPU by any method, not only the engine's.
How much of the GPU's top memory speed a part reaches while it runs.
Gigabytes a second: how fast memory is read.
How much of the GPU's top maths speed a part uses.
One piece of code the GPU runs. A step of the model is hundreds of them.
Time between GPU kernels, when the GPU waits for the next piece of work.
A tool that watches the GPU and notes when every kernel starts and ends. Watching slows the run a little.
The run with no recording tool attached: the speed the engine really has.
The same setup run several times, so a later change can be told apart from normal variation.
How the model's numbers are stored: fewer bits per number means less to read and a faster step, at some cost in accuracy.
What the model keeps about earlier tokens (keys and values), read again for every new token.
The part of the model that looks back at earlier tokens.
The largest part of each layer: two big matrix steps on every token.
Layers that carry a running summary of the conversation instead of looking back at every token.
The engine recording its GPU steps once and replaying them, which saves start-up time per step.
The program that runs the model (llama.cpp, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM or tinygrad).
The engine's version. The pin is the version BoltBeam was last checked against; upstream is the newest release.
The GPU driver and libraries the engine was built with.
Multi-token prediction: the model guesses a few tokens ahead and checks them in one step; acceptance is how many guesses were right.
Parts timed one at a time outside the engine, then scaled so they add up to the real run's time.

no_limit.formula_refused: There is no limit for this run yet: BoltBeam cannot yet work out the fastest this GPU allows for a model with these state-space layers.
no_limit.speculative: No percentage of the limit is shown: this run drafted tokens ahead and checked several in one step, and the limit is for one token per step.
no_limit.no_matrix_rate: There is no limit for this run yet: this GPU's speed for one kind of math this model uses has not been measured yet.

cache_ram.changes: turns off llama-server's prompt cache in host RAM (8 GiB by default), which saves the previous request's whole state to RAM before each new prompt starts: about 80 ms for a 10,000-token prompt on one model (measured), outside the engine's prompt timer. The cost: switching between conversations reads their shared start again; a conversation's own checkpoints still work
cache_ram.tight: RAM is tight: the experts in RAM and the 8 GiB cache are more than the {usable} GB usable
cache_ram.one_shot: one-shot prompts (no conversation comes back to an earlier start); with plenty of RAM and returning conversations, keep the default
cache_ram.report: This server kept its prompt cache in RAM (the default), which saves the previous request's state before each prompt; that is part of the time outside its timer.

outside_timer.line: The engine's own timer leaves {outside} ms outside it; timed {timed}, the same prompt takes {wall} ms ({wall_tok_s} tok/s).

timed.client: by the client from request sent to reply received
timed.vllm: around vLLM's own generate call, in the same process

prompt_kind.random_tokens_moe_capture: The split of time by part above was recorded on random token ids. These send a model's tokens to many more of its expert parts than real text does. So it is not the split of the turns the server really ran.
prompt_kind.random_tokens_moe: Measured on random token ids, which send this model's tokens to many more of its expert parts than real text does: the speed reads low, about half on one model, and is not its speed on text. BoltBeam normally measures this on real text; it did not here.

prompt_form.ids: The prompt was sent as token ids, with no chat template around it.
prompt_form.chat: The prompt was sent as a chat request, the way a chat app sends it: the model's chat template wraps the text, and the server may split the first batch where the user message starts.

time_budget.line: Where the {wall} ms of the traced request (under the profiler) went: GPU kernels {kernels} ms, copies with no kernel running {exposed} ms, GPU idle {idle} ms, host time before and after the GPU work {host} ms.
time_budget.line_unfit: Where the {wall} ms of the traced request (under the profiler) went: GPU kernels {kernels} ms, copies with no kernel running {exposed} ms, GPU idle {idle} ms; the host time before and after the GPU work is unknown. These do not add up: the trace's GPU work ({window} ms) is longer than the request's wall time, so the trace holds more than this one request.
time_budget.line_no_wall: Where the {window} ms of GPU work went: GPU kernels {kernels} ms, copies with no kernel running {exposed} ms, GPU idle {idle} ms. The request's own wall time was not recorded, so the host time outside the GPU work is not known.
time_budget.sums: These add up to the wall time within {tol} ms.
time_budget.residual: The GPU work fits inside the request's wall time; the host time is what is left of the wall, so the parts add up to it by how they are counted.
time_budget.no_rows: BoltBeam has no kernel family rows for {engines}: its kernels are counted by the GPU vendor's rows or as other kernels.
time_budget.unattributed: These parts leave {ms} ms of the wall time unaccounted for.
time_budget.over: The parts exceed the wall by {ms} ms.
time_budget.trace_longer: The trace's GPU work runs {ms} ms longer than the request's wall time: the trace holds more than this one request.
time_budget.small_gaps: {ms} ms is in {n} short gaps under {threshold} ms each

families.output_layer: the output layer (the last matmul before the result is read)
families.row_gather: row gathers (embedding rows, per-layer embeddings, picked expert weights)

decode.refused: This decode request is not attributed: {why}.
decode.counts: The engine's counts: {steps_expected} steps after the prompt, so {mains_expected} forwards of the model, {catchups_expected} catch-up passes of the draft head and {drafts_expected} draft passes ({drafted} tokens drafted); the trace holds {forwards_found} forwards, {prompt_forwards} of them the prompt's (read before the first token arrived), the rest with {layers_found} per-layer kernels each.
decode.steps: The decode: {steps} steps for the {tokens} tokens after the prompt's, {per_token} ms a token (a step {median} ms median, {low} to {high}), with {drafts} passes of the draft head ({catchups} of them catch-ups); the prompt took {prompt} ms and the time after the last step {tail} ms.
decode.check_ok: The forwards found match the engine's own counts: {mains} of the model ({steps} steps after the prompt), {catchups} catch-up passes and {drafts} draft passes ({drafted} tokens drafted).
decode.prompt_from_counts: No first-token mark was recorded, so the prompt is the first {n} forwards: the fewest after which the rest give the engine's counts. The count check is weaker for it (it chose the cut); a capture with the driver's --first-token-mark is not.
decode.drafts_inside: This engine runs its draft passes inside the step, with no result read between them, so their time is in the step's kernels and not told apart.
decode.parts: The verify forwards' kernels {verify}%, the draft passes' kernels {draft}%, copies with no kernel running {exposed}%.
decode.idle: GPU idle by what the host was doing: {causes}.
decode.input: Input copies, {what}: {n} copies, {bytes} bytes a token; {copy} ms a token of copy with no kernel running and {before} ms a token of GPU idle right before them, the host gathering the rows ({pct}% of the decode time).
decode.input_other: Input copies, {what}: {n} copies, {bytes} bytes a token; {copy} ms a token of copy with no kernel running ({pct}% of the decode time).

inputs.per_layer_token_embd: per-layer embedding rows (each copy a whole number of the model's per-layer embedding rows and of no other input's)
inputs.token_embd: token embedding rows (each copy a whole number of the model's token embedding rows and of no other input's)
inputs.draft_hidden: the draft head's hidden rows (each copy a whole number of them and of no other input's)
inputs.ambiguous: host-to-GPU copies whose size fits more than one input's rows, so not named as any
inputs.unidentified: other host-to-GPU copies, not identified (token ids, positions and the like)

decode.input_rows: The copies are matched by size against a token's row of each input (bytes): {rows}; the {element} bytes an element are the engine's gather output (its decode row's host_rows_element_bytes), an engine fact, not read from the model file.
decode.held_more: {n} draft forwards each hold more than one draft pass's kernels (the build ran them with no result read between); each is counted as the passes it holds.
decode.streamed: Each request was streamed, to mark its first token; the same request unstreamed right after decoded {pct}% against it (more than 0: streaming slowed it).
decode.streamed_unmeasured: Each request was streamed, to mark its first token; what streaming does to the decode is not measured in this run (no unstreamed control: --stream-control).
decode.constants: Fixed, not derived: the sums check's allowance {tolerance}; the display cuts {display_cuts}; idle gaps: {gap_ms}.
decode.bound: What bounds a token: reading the weights at the measured {gbs} GB/s ({source}) takes {weight} ms of each token's {per_token} ms ({share}%); the other {rest} ms a token is the rest: kernel time beyond that read, idle and copies. The bytes: {how}.
decode.bound_missing: What bounds a token is not derived: {why}.
decode.overhead_missing: The capture overhead is not measured: {why}. Every time above is under the profiler.

why.no_steps: the engine's counts leave no decode step after the prompt
why.no_first_token: the driver did not record when the first token arrived (--first-token-mark), so the prompt's forwards cannot be told
why.prompt_unmatched: no forward of the trace ends before the first token arrived: the span or the clock is off
why.no_decode_row: BoltBeam has no decode row for this engine (data/kernel_families.json engines.<engine>.decode), so its forwards cannot be counted
why.forwards_unmatched: the forwards in the trace do not give the engine's own counts (a draft pass run and not counted, as one whose token fell under p_min, or forwards in a shape that is not whole draft passes), so the span or the cut is off and no share is said
why.residency_not_read: where the weights went was not read (the driver's --residency-probe), so the GPU's read rate may not cover them
why.no_read: no measured read rate or weight bytes were given (--model and --target)
why.no_draft_bytes: the draft head's weight bytes are not known (--draft)
why.not_all_on_gpu: the server's load log says not every weight is on the GPU (layers left on the CPU, or tensors placed in host RAM), and the GPU's read rate does not cover reading them
why.no_engine_line: the driver output has no engine line for this draft count, so where the weights were is not known
why.no_untraced: no untraced run of this request was given (--untraced)
why.untraced_no_row: the untraced run has no request at this draft count and depth

time_budget.copy: {direction} copies from {memory} on GPU queue {stream}: {gb} GB in {busy} ms ({gbs} GB/s), {exposed} ms with no kernel running.

memories.managed: memory shared by the host and the GPU

rows.host: host time outside the GPU work
rows.wall: wall time of the traced request (under the profiler)

page.title: Where the time went
page.of: the {length}-token prompt's traced request (under the profiler), from its GPU trace
page.queues: A GPU queue (a stream) runs its work in order; copies and kernels on different queues can overlap. Pinned host memory is locked in RAM, so the GPU reads it directly; ordinary (pageable) memory is first staged through a pinned buffer.
page.copies_overlap: Copies on different GPU queues overlap each other, so their times with no kernel running add up to more than the copy total.
page.window_not_fit: The GPU work in this trace ({window} ms) is longer than the traced request's wall time ({wall} ms): the trace holds more than this one request, so the parts do not add up to the wall and the host time outside the GPU work is unknown.
page.no_wall: The request's own wall time was not recorded, so the parts add up to the GPU work ({window} ms), not to a wall time.
page.only_one: this run has no time budget (a prefill capture writes one).

not_split.not_run: The time is not split into parts yet: timing each part has not run for this run.
not_split.not_split: The time could not be split into parts on this run; only the whole step is measured.
not_split.no_matrix_rate: The time is not split into parts: this GPU's speed for one kind of math this model uses has not been measured yet, so those parts have no limit.
not_split.tensor_parallel: The time is not split into parts: that is not built yet for a model spread over several GPUs this way.

head_to_head.by_wall: Prompt speed and time are wall times, because each engine's own prompt timer leaves out different things: a server's from request sent to reply received, vLLM's around its generate call in the same process. Turning text into tokens is outside both, because each engine was sent token ids.
head_to_head.by_wall_mixed: Prompt speed and time are wall times, because each engine's own prompt timer leaves out different things: a server's from request sent to reply received, vLLM's around its generate call in the same process.
head_to_head.other_prompts: The two runs read different prompts ({a} against {b}), so neither time says which engine is faster, and no winner is marked.
head_to_head.other_forms: The two runs sent the prompt in different forms ({a} against {b}). A chat request adds the chat template and can change how the server splits the prompt. So neither time says which engine is faster, and no winner is marked.
head_to_head.by_wall_chat: Prompt speed and time are wall times, because each engine's own prompt timer leaves out different things: a server's from request sent to reply received, vLLM's around its generate call in the same process. Each engine was sent the prompt as a chat request: a server turns the text into tokens inside its wall time, vLLM's driver before its generate call.
head_to_head.not_by_wall: Prompt speed and time are each engine's own timer here, and engines define their timer differently: one run has no client wall time, so do not read a small gap between them as a win.
head_to_head.same: Same model, GPU, engine, build, weights and settings.
head_to_head.unlisted: a build BoltBeam does not know by name
head_to_head.not_measured: Not compared: {run} has no measured result yet.
head_to_head.parts_other_model: The parts line up only between two runs of the same model, so only the headline figures are side by side.
head_to_head.parts_differ: The parts line up only between two runs of the same model on the same GPU, engine and work; these differ in {field}, so only the headline figures are side by side.

mtp.name: the draft layer
mtp.what: Changes only the draft layer, which guesses a few words ahead for the model to check (MTP). The model checks every guess, so only the speed with drafts on is measured.
mtp.why_range: The speed with drafts on is timed on the original, the copy and the original again, once for each number of drafts it tries; how many it tries decides where in that range it ends.
